meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It even still smells of ink.
They even closed the restaurant for us.
Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Извините, но я решил остаться в ресторане.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but I decided to stay at the restaurant.
We are changing the restaurant's concept.
This is a restaurant of auteur cuisine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: For a starter it will do.

examples.text: Ты пойми, для нее это важно.
examples.trans: Understand, for her it is important.
They even closed the restaurant for us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are changing the restaurant's concept.

examples.text: Может, мы пока старое меню оставим?
examples.trans: Maybe we should keep the old menu for now?

examples.text: Вы еще меня благодарить будете, когда мы звезду получим.
examples.trans: You will thank me yet when we get the star.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: Нет, ресторан закрыли, шефа будут снимать.
examples.trans: No, they closed the restaurant, they are going to film the chef.

examples.text: Я не поняла, почему ресторан закрыт?
examples.trans: I do not understand, why is the restaurant closed?
They even closed the restaurant for us.

meanings.en: to take a seat, to sit down
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'саживаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'take a seat', paired with 'присесть'.

related.gloss: not to take a seat (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Please, have a seat.
He sits down on the edge of the chair.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Please take a seat.
A coffee, please.
Thank you! — You're welcome.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.
It was an interesting movie, right?
Well yes, bye.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.text: У вас сначала у родителей разрешение просить надо.
examples.trans: In your country you first have to ask the parents for permission.
Yes, first I will order some ribs.
First they were rude and insulting over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.trans: Maybe we should order?
We ordered tea and sandwiches.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'ribs' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть рёбрышко.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always ribs.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vitya, this is my restaurant!
This is my restaurant!

examples.text: Это мой ресторан, и я решаю, что здесь едят.
examples.trans: This is my restaurant, and I decide what people eat here.

meanings.note: Indeclinable neuter noun borrowed from French 'menu' (detailed list, from Latin 'minutus').

examples.trans: Otherwise I will die before my time.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

examples.trans: There is no old menu, there is only the new menu.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe I really should quit this madhouse?

examples.trans: Let's go for a walk tomorrow.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('yesterday's meal').

examples.text: Тем более он еще за вчерашнее не заплатил.

examples.text: Ты что здесь делаешь? После вчерашнего!

examples.text: Тем более он еще за вчерашнее не заплатил.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть пищеварение.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'вольнять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'уволить'.

examples.text: Либо ты его увольняешь, либо я закрываю ресторан!

examples.text: Витя, тебе вовсе не обязательно увольняться.

examples.text: Я не знаю, я ничего не понял.

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ё-таки').

examples.trans: He came after all.
Maybe we'll go after all?

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it's time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In my opinion, it is time to go.

examples.text: Ну что, думаешь, пора уже с Катей поговорить?
examples.trans: Well, do you think it is time to talk to Katya already?
Are you arguing over what to treat us with?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'drop by, stop in'.

examples.text: Я заехал сказать, что мэр вами недоволен.
examples.trans: I stopped by to say that the mayor is dissatisfied with you.

examples.text: Надо заехать домой, принять душ, переодеться.
examples.trans: I need to stop by home, take a shower, change.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: I want to say something important.

examples.text: Он сказал, что половину слов в меню не понял.
examples.trans: He said that he did not understand half the words on the menu.

examples.text: Миша, ты меня прости, что я тогда Элеоноре ничего не сказал.
examples.trans: Misha, forgive me for not saying anything to Eleonora back then.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is the occasion?
What does that mean?

examples.text: Прости, что-то я удержаться не смог.
examples.trans: Sorry, somehow I could not hold back.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'maire' (from Latin 'maior', greater/senior official).

examples.trans: Do I have an inspection from city hall?

examples.text: А вот заместитель мэра у нас проверку устраивает.
examples.trans: Here the deputy mayor is conducting an inspection at our place.

examples.text: Я заехал сказать, что мэр вами недоволен.
examples.trans: I stopped by to say that the mayor is dissatisfied with you.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'довольный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dissatisfied').

examples.trans: He is always dissatisfied.

examples.text: Славик, ну ты вечно всем недоволен!
examples.trans: Slavik, you are always dissatisfied with everything!
I see, the landlady was very unhappy.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe I really should quit this madhouse?
Otherwise I will die before my time.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'странять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'suspends / removes'.

examples.text: И он отстраняет вас от должности.
examples.trans: And he is removing you from office.

examples.text: Как отстраняет, я что-то не понял?
examples.trans: What do you mean removing me, I do not understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe I really should quit this madhouse?
I agree to work for you.

examples.text: Не знаю, я на экран не смотрел особо.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not really look at the screen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'post / office' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И он отстраняет вас от должности.
examples.trans: And he is removing you from office.
The job is waiting.
It's a good position.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is the staff meeting about anyway?

examples.text: Я же не знаю, как у вас принято за девушками ухаживать.
examples.trans: I do not know how it is customary in your country to court girls.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Прости, что-то я удержаться не смог.
examples.trans: Sorry, somehow I could not hold back.

examples.text: Как отстраняет, я что-то не понял?
examples.trans: What do you mean removing me, I do not understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, я ничего не понял.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not understand anything.

examples.text: Он сказал, что половину слов в меню не понял.
examples.trans: He said that he did not understand half the words on the menu.

examples.text: Я не понял, она у нас работает?
examples.trans: I do not understand, does she work here with us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She will even thank you afterward.

Thank you for dinner.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you for dinner.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на ужин?
